project_title: Print Designer needed — production artwork files for luxury pareo brand

project_metadata.job_title: Print Designer needed — production artwork files for luxury pareo brand
project_metadata.job_description:
I need production-ready artwork files created for 2 pareo designs for a luxury label launching later this year.
The 2 designs:
1. Diagonal basket weave repeat (matchstick/rattan style) — reference image provided
2. Zebra print (gold/camel base, bold black stripes) — reference image provided
The work is really in building the two repeat prints to match the provided references.
Specs:
	•	Size: 110 × 180cm
	•	Format: Print-ready PDF/X or TIFF, CMYK, 150dpi minimum
	•	Turnaround: 3-5 days
Please share portfolio samples of any textile, print, or surface design work when applying.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hi Ornella,

Thanks so much for coming back to me!

At this stage we are leaning toward digital printing, mainly for pareos and textile accessories. The overall direction is refined, artisanal and luxury resort focused - natural textures, woven references and imperfect details rather than anything too polished or overly graphic.

Ive attached the reference imagery so you can get a better sense of the diagonal basket weave direction and overall feel. We definitely want it to feel elevated and organic rather than flat and have that textural element.

We are hoping we can enlarge these (or use them as references) to create our own textile print. IS this possible? We also want to create 2 x block colour pareos using the mustard / burgandy colours in that reference attached too with the black border. But keen to get your help first on the Zebra & woven print.

Completely understand on timing too — quality is the priority for us so we’d rather allow the right amount of time to get the final files feeling considered and production ready.

Let me know what you think

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Thank you so much for sharing the references and for the context on the direction, it really helps to understand the world you're building.
Great news on both counts. The diagonal basket weave is completely achievable, and your references give me exactly what I need to work from. What I'd do is build the texture manually in Procreate, which gives that handmade, imperfect quality you're describing, organic, artisanal, elevated. I'd then use the reference image as a texture overlay to pull that specific rattan grain into the illustration, so the final print carries the feel of the original without just being a scaled photo. From there I'd resolve the seamless repeat technically in Photoshop and Illustrator to make sure the file arrives production ready.
For the zebra, the references are clear and I love the direction! Bold, fluid stripes on that gold/camel base reads really luxurious. That one I can approach as a looser, more gestural illustration to keep it feeling alive rather than flat.
Let's get started with the zebra and the basket weave then! Once both are approved and you're happy with the direction, we can move straight into the block colour pareos.
In terms of timing, I'd propose 7 business days for both prints. Around day 3 or 4 I'd share an intermediate check-in so you can see the direction before the final files, and if there's anything to adjust my process includes 2 additional revision rounds from there. I always aim to keep the total time as short as possible without rushing the detail work!
One last question, do you know what fabric you'll be printing on? Silk, viscose and cotton each have slightly different colour profile requirements for digital print, and I want to make sure the CMYK files are calibrated for your specific supplier.
Looking forward to this one!

Hi Phoebe!
Attached you'll find the Milestone 1 PDF with all the prints developed so far. Here's a summary of what's included and what I need from you to move forward!
1\. What's included in this delivery
Basket Weave print in two texture versions, Frottage and Reference-Based, each with two scales. Zebra print in three directional options, Noir, Savanna and Gold Skin, each shown at tile detail and full repeat scale. Two block colour pareos, Rooibos Tea and Sudan Brown, each with two border scale options, Slim and Full. All mockups are shown at 110 x 180 cm as reference.
Full resolution repeat files are available here for your review: <https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1DOsO-ZQ_6MK-nSQKCBqWlUPanCcAsk0F?usp=drive_link>
2\. Your choices, what I need from you
Which Zebra direction do you prefer, 01 Noir, 02 Savanna or 03 Gold Skin? Which Basket Weave texture do you prefer, Frottage or Reference-Based? For the block colour pareos, which border scale works better for your collection, Slim or Full? Please use the measurements shown in the PDF as reference when evaluating each option, they reflect real scale on fabric.
3\. A note on colour, screen vs fabric
The warm golden tones, especially in the Gold Skin zebra variant, will appear slightly more matte on fabric than on screen. This is normal for pigment printing on voile and is not a loss of quality, it's just how the material reads the colour. I wanted you to know this before production so there are no surprises!
4\. What I need to move forward with final files
Confirmation of your fabric supplier's ICC profile for CMYK calibration. Confirmation of exact Pantone references with your supplier if available. Final seam allowance measurements you need added to the digital files before production. Any additional modifications or notes on the selected prints.
5\. Timeline for Milestone 2
Once I have your feedback and selections, I'll work toward May 29 as the Milestone 2 deadline. If I finish earlier, I'll send everything before that date!
Looking forward to hearing your thoughts!
Orne

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hey Orne,

Thank you for pulling these together. I think the direction is definitely getting there, but I have a few notes to refine the colours \+ scale so it feels softer and more elevated/TELA MARE.

With the references we shared, we were aiming for something naturally aged and tonal. At the moment, the artwork is feeling slightly too clean/saturated, so we’d love to introduce more softness, depth and irregularity so the prints feel more collected and textural rather than overly graphic.

Overall, I think both prints would benefit from:
\* less contrast
\* more grain
\* more texture overlay
\* slightly faded edges
\* less of a “perfect vector” feeling

Zebra print:
\* Right now the zebra is reading a little too yellow/gold and slightly high contrast.
\* I’d love the gold toned down into more of a soft bronze / sandy caramel tone instead.
\* The overall feeling should feel more sun-faded, vintage and expensive rather than bright or overly golden.
\* I think the larger, more organic stripe direction is strongest.

Weave print:
\* The weave is currently pulling slightly too orange/red.
\* I’d love this shifted into a softer brushed brown tone with more depth and less warmth.
\* we prefer the scale of the larger 5cm diagonal weave — so ideally we combine:
→ the colour/tone of the smaller weave
→ with the larger scale of the 5cm version.

Overall, everything can come back slightly softer, more tonal and more lived-in - less polished/saturated and more natural, earthy and collected.

I think once the tones are adjusted we’ll be really close!
